newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-LISBON EX-SOCCER BOSS SAYS REFEREES BRIBED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LISBON EX-SOCCER BOSS SAYS REFEREES BRIBED.

text.p: A disgraced former chairman of Sporting, one of Portugal's leading soccer sides, said on Monday that he had bribed referees during his time at the club in the late 1980s.
Jorge Goncalves, who fled Portugal for Angola to avoid charges of tax evasion, said that bribery had been widespread amongst leading teams.

"I had to reach a financial agreement with certain people to help get the right results, mainly when playing against other teams that did the same thing," he said in an interview in Angola with Portuguese TSF radio.
Portuguese soccer has been rocked recently by a series of allegations of bribery.

The chairman of reigning league champions Porto, Jorge Nuno Pinto da Costa, and two fellow directors are being investigated by police over accusations that the club paid for a leading referee to take a holiday in Brazil in 1995.
Goncalves, who was Sporting chairman between 1988 and 1989, refused to identify anybody involved in bribery. "I am a long way away in Angola and they have children," he said in the interview.
Amounts paid could range from $30,000 for an international game, to $3,000 in Portugal, depending on the match and the resources of the club, the former chairman said.
